evidence_items.summary: TinyML achieves ML inference under a milliWatt, enabling battery-powered always-on applications.
evidence_items.notes: Authors cite TinyML Foundation [1] for this definition.

evidence_items.summary: MLPerf Tiny measures accuracy, latency, and energy of ML inference.
MLPerf Tiny v0.5 benchmark suite includes four benchmarks: keyword spotting, visual wake words, image classification, and anomaly detection.

locator.anchor: Table 1: MLPerf Tiny v0.5 Inference Benchmarks

evidence_items.summary: Keyword Spotting uses Speech Commands v2 dataset: 105,829 utterances from 2,618 speakers, 30 words, under Creative Commons BY.
Visual Wake Words uses MSCOCO 2014 dataset; images resized to 96x96; person must occupy >2.5% of image.
Image Classification uses CIFAR-10: 60,000 32x32x3 RGB images, 10 classes, 6,000 images per class.
Anomaly Detection uses DCASE2020 dataset (combining ToyADMOS and MIMII); benchmark uses Toy-car subset; training on 7 toy-cars, 1,000 samples each.
KWS model is a depthwise-separable CNN (DS-CNN) with 38.6K parameters, TFLite model size 52.5 KB.
DS-CNN achieves 92.2% accuracy on Speech Commands v2 in authors' experiments.
evidence_items.conditions: KWS, DS-CNN, full test set, authors' experiments
evidence_items.notes: No variance, seed count, or run count reported.

evidence_items.summary: Quantized DS-CNN achieves 91.6% accuracy on full KWS test set and 91.7% on 1,000-utterance subset.
evidence_items.conditions: KWS, quantized DS-CNN, Speech Commands v2

evidence_items.summary: KWS quality target set at 90% top-1 accuracy to allow for quantization variation.
VWW model is MobileNetV1 with alpha=0.25, 96x96 input, 2 output classes, TFLite model size 325 KB.
VWW MobileNetV1 achieves approximately 86% accuracy on preprocessed MSCOCO 2014 test dataset.
VWW quality target is 80% top-1 accuracy on MSCOCO 2014 test dataset.
IC model is a customized ResNetv1 with 3 residual stacks (vs 4 in official ResNet), 32x32x3 input, 10-class output, TFLite model size 96 KB.
IC ResNet reference model achieves 86.5% accuracy on 200-image CIFAR-10 test subset.
evidence_items.conditions: IC, custom ResNetv1, 200-image subset of CIFAR-10 test set

evidence_items.summary: IC quality target is 85% top-1 accuracy.
AD model is a fully-connected autoencoder: input/output size 640; encoder and decoder each have four 128-unit FC layers with BatchNorm and ReLU; bottleneck size 8. TFLite model size 270 KB.

AD anomaly score is computed as the average MSE of reconstruction errors over a sliding window of 5 frames over the central 6.4-second portion of 10-second audio; input is log-mel-spectrogram with 128 bands and 32ms frame size.
AD fp32 reference model achieves AUC of 0.88; quantized version achieves AUC of 0.86; quality target set to AUC 0.85.
evidence_items.conditions: AD, FC-autoencoder, 248-sample evaluation set (normal and anomalous from 4 machines)

evidence_items.summary: AD evaluation uses 248 samples of normal and anomalous sounds from 4 different machines; metric is AUC-ROC (parameterless, no threshold required).
Reference implementations run on NUCLEO-L4R5ZI board using TFLite for Microcontrollers (TFLM) in TFLite format; built with bare-metal MBED and GCC-ARM toolchain.
Latency measurement protocol: five trials, each running inference for minimum 10 seconds and 10 iterations; score is median IPS across five runs.
Energy measurement: identical to latency but additionally measures total energy; score is µJ/inference (median of 5 runs).

Energy measurement hardware: electrical-isolation proxy (IO Manager, Arduino UNO), energy monitor (EMON) — supports STMicro LPM01A, Jetperch Joulescope JS110, Keysight N6705; only power to core is measured.

First round (v0.5, June 2021) received 5 diverse submissions: ARM MCU (TFLM baseline), RISC-V MCU, Raspberry Pi 4 (software toolchain), neural network accelerator (Syntiant TDK), and FPGA (hls4ml, open division).
INT-8 post-training quantization is the most common numerical format across v0.5 submissions.

value.observation: INT-8 PTQ most common in v0.5 submissions

evidence_items.summary: No v0.5 submission modified the training dataset; TinyML design is still largely model, framework, and hardware focused.
Power consumption of v0.5 platforms ranged from µWatts to Watts.
Closed division: submitters must use the same models, datasets, and quality targets as the reference; only post-training quantization (PTQ) is permitted; no retraining or weight replacement.
Open division: submitters may change model, training scripts, and dataset; must use same test dataset for accuracy but need not meet accuracy threshold.
Streaming inputs and pre-processing are excluded from the measurement window; limited bandwidth between host PC and DUT prevents realistic streaming scenarios.

value.limitation: no streaming in measurement; pre-processing excluded

evidence_items.summary: Closed division reference models primarily use FC and CNN layers; RNN and other architectures not yet in closed division.

value.limitation: no RNNs or non-FC/CNN architectures in closed division reference

evidence_items.summary: Excluding pre-processing creates a degenerate case risk: a submitter could define almost the entire model as 'feature extraction'.

value.limitation: pre-processing exclusion creates degenerate feature-extraction boundary risk

evidence_items.summary: CoreMark does not profile full ML inference programs; MLMark models require gigabytes of memory; MLPerf inference precludes MCU-class devices.

value.gap: no existing benchmark fits TinyML requirements

evidence_items.summary: Benchmark suite is developed by more than 50 organizations from industry and academia.
DUT firmware API requires: timestamp function (1ms resolution for latency; GPIO toggle for energy), UART Tx/Rx, input tensor loading, single inference function, output printing function.
The benchmark has already acted as a standard set of tasks for TinyML research and been made into public projects on a TinyML development platform.

value.observation: adopted as tasks for TinyML research [4]; public projects on development platform [16]

evidence_items.notes: Authors cite Banbury et al. [4] (MicroNets) and Moreau [16] (Edge Impulse) as examples.
